Return $d = \min(\max(d_{xy}, d_z), 0) + \text{length}(\max(d_{xy}, d_z, 0))$ [S1, unofficial].

The claim provides a mathematical formula for the signed distance function (SDF) of a hexagonal prism: $d = min(max(d_{xy}, d_z), 0) + length(max(d_{xy}, d_z, 0))$. Source [S1] contains the GLSL code for `sdHexPrism` which implements exactly this logic: `return min(max(d.x,d.y),0.0) + length(max(d,0.0));`. Here, `d.x` corresponds to the distance to the hexagonal cross-section ($d_{xy}$) and `d.y` corresponds to the distance to the height ($d_z$). The Python implementation in the same source also confirms this structure with `return -relu(-maximum(*unconcat(q))) + length(relu(q))`, which is mathematically equivalent to the min/max/length formula provided in the claim. All facts in the claim are present and supported by the evidence.
